newsitem.title: USA: Ohio's soil moisture 84 pct short to very short.
newsitem.headline: Ohio's soil moisture 84 pct short to very short.

text.p: Weekend rains brought some relief to dry Ohio fields in the northeast third of the state but topsoil moisture was rated short to very short across most of the state, Agricultural Statistics Service said.
Topsoil moisture was rated 84 percent short to very short, compared with 69 percent last week.
Crop conditions declined as a result of the poor soil moisture. Corn was rated seven percent very poor, 18 percent poor, 39 percent fair, 31 good and five percent excellent.
Soybeans were rated seven percent very poor, 18 percent poor, 40 fair, 30 percent good and five percent excellent.

Development was also slow as 79 percent of the corn crop had reached the dough stage, compared with the five-year average of 99 percent. Twenty-two percent had reached the dent stage, against 73 percent average.
Corn development was two weeks behind average.
Two percent of the soybeans had dropped leaves, down sharply from average of 28 percent.
Soybean development was also two weeks behind average.
Pasture was rated 14 percent very poor, 29 percent poor, 37 percent fair, 19 percent good and one percent excellent.
